comments.body:
PLAN REVISED after a BLOCK verdict from review-plan. Re-review follows.

THE BLOCKING FINDING WAS A REAL PRODUCTION DEFECT, independently confirmed by direct probe before the
review returned: isinstance(JiraDataCenterBackend(transport=...), Backend) is FALSE on merged main.
The Backend @runtime_checkable Protocol requires nine members; the DC backend defines seven and is
missing query_project and assert_env_ready. Cloud's JiraBackend has both (adapters/jira/backend.py:162
and :169). Probed:

    vendor True | project True | query_project False | assert_env_ready False

This is not test bookkeeping. query_project is the READ scope the inbound fetcher scopes its search to
and FAILS CLOSED on when empty (bug 626d) — absent, a DC inbound pass raises AttributeError.
assert_env_ready is the fail-fast raising the neutral BackendEnvError naming a missing connection
essential before bootstrap-band execution (ticket 97f2). J6's registry test passed while the backend
does not satisfy the port; adding it to the contract fixture is exactly what surfaces this. backend.py
was NOT in Scope — it now is, and the fix goes in the backend, with no contract assertion weakened.

ALSO ADDRESSED from the 8 advisories, each verified against the tree rather than taken on faith:
 * tests/unit/test_config_reconciler_backend.py EXISTS (2.5K) and is the right home for the new
   jira-datacenter load + env-override cases; added to Scope. Its existing
   test_unknown_backend_rejected_at_config_load asserts '"jira" in str(exc.value)', which still holds
   after the widening, so it needs no edit.
 * The live reconcile pass needs a local store/git/config that the DC harness conftest does not
   provision. SETTLED, not deferred: rebar_repo is defined in tests/external/conftest.py:159 — the
   PARENT conftest — so tests/external/live_jira_dc/ inherits it by ordinary pytest conftest
   inheritance. No rebar_repo-equivalent is to be written.
 * The FakeTransport question is DECIDED rather than left as 'check before adding': reuse the existing
   FakeTransport (no contract assertion calls probe_remote, and SupportsAbsenceProbe conformance comes
   from the BACKEND's probe_remote, not the transport's), adding a one-line probe_remote to it; no
   rival DC-specific fake.
 * AC8's 'explicit log assertion' now names its artifact and mechanism: caplog at WARNING+, asserting
   no record carries exc_info and none matches Traceback|Unhandled|unexpected error.
 * The provenance oracle is pinned to the live module (only a real pass produces a genuinely DC-created
   ticket).
 * New ACs for the config-load and env-override cases (previously described work with no covering AC)
   and for a transport error surfacing rather than being swallowed into a converged pass.

_optionality.yml verified safe to tighten: 'jira' is declared ONLY in the jira-datacenter extra
(pyproject.toml:168); base dependencies are pyyaml/jsonschema/referencing, and the 'jira' at
pyproject.toml:24 is a KEYWORD, not a dependency.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
PLAN REVISED A SECOND TIME. Re-review #2 BLOCKED with two findings; both were MY errors, introduced
by the first revision, and both are confirmed correct by direct inspection rather than taken on faith.

BLOCKING 1 — the caplog mechanism I invented is INFEASIBLE. I specified asserting zero unhandled
exceptions via pytest's caplog. But rebar.reconcile() runs the reconciler in a SUBPROCESS
(subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True), src/rebar/_lib_ops.py:114). caplog hooks only the TEST
process's logging and can never see a subprocess's records. Worse, on the success path reconcile()
returns parsed stdout JSON and DISCARDS stderr entirely (it is surfaced only when returncode is not in
(0, 75), where it is raised inside RebarError). So the AC as written could never have been satisfied.
REPLACED with a mechanism that works: the live test invokes the reconciler subprocess directly using
the same argv _lib_ops.reconcile builds ([sys.executable, '-m', 'rebar_reconciler', '--mode', M,
'--repo-root', R] under engine_env) with capture_output=True, and asserts returncode == 0,
'Traceback' not in stderr, and mutation_failures == 0 in the parsed stdout envelope.

BLOCKING 2 — I solved only HALF the live-test provisioning problem. I correctly established that
rebar_repo is inherited from the PARENT conftest (tests/external/conftest.py:159), then declared the
matter 'settled'. It was not: that fixture calls rebar.init_repo() and writes NO
[tool.rebar.reconciler] config, so the reconcile subprocess would have had no backend, no base_url and
no credential — failing at config-load or silently driving the CLOUD backend. The plan now specifies
the wiring:
  * write a rebar.toml into the rebar_repo root with [reconciler] backend='jira-datacenter',
    base_url=<harness URL>, and allow_insecure=true. The last is REQUIRED, not optional: the harness is
    http://localhost:2990/jira (conftest.py:56, JIRA_DC_BASE_URL-overridable) and J6's TLS validator
    REJECTS a non-https base_url at config-load unless allow_insecure is set. Plus [jira] project=
    <jira_dc_project>, which is where resolve_jira_datacenter_settings() reads the project.
  * monkeypatch.setenv('JIRA_PAT', jira_dc_pat) — the fixture returns a raw token STRING and sets no
    env var itself. Verified this reaches the child: rebar._engine.engine_env builds the subprocess
    environment as dict(os.environ) (_engine.py:93).

ALSO FIXED: the transport-failure AC no longer says 'propagate OR be explicitly reported' (two
behaviours, incompatible assertion styles) — it is PROPAGATION only, asserted with pytest.raises. Added
an explicit AC for FakeTransport.probe_remote and its delegation. Split the three 'and'-bundled
criteria so each is independently verifiable (8 -> 15 ACs).

ONE ADVISORY DELIBERATELY NOT ACTIONED, because its premise is factually wrong. It asked for
depends_on edges to the cited prerequisites (62d9, aac8, 0a94, c97f, 9fd4), claiming b4e3 'neither
declares depends_on nor is blocked by' them. It IS blocked by them: 9fd4 blocks b4e3 DIRECTLY, and the
others reach it transitively (c97f blocks 9fd4; 62d9 blocks aac8). Attempting each forward edge is
correctly rejected by rebar itself: 'would create a cycle at story level', 5 for 5. The dependency
chain is already recorded, in the opposite direction. Adding the requested edges would corrupt the
graph, so it stays as it is.

  apply_inbound_records.py: vendor = select_backend(load_config()).vendor

  creation_channel='jira-datacenter' ext=acct-dc    -> ValueError: invalid creation_channel

It only reproduces on a FRESH mint — an existing (provider, external_id) mapping is reused idempotently
and never reaches validation. My first probe reused an identity and showed a FALSE PASS; distinct
external_ids exposed it.

'except Exception:  # best-effort ghost mint; never fail the inbound apply' and logged at DEBUG. So
every inbound DC ghost-identity mint fails, is swallowed, and the pass still converges. That is exactly
epic AC6's premise — a swallowed exception can still converge, so convergence is not evidence.

FIX DIRECTION, and the one explicitly rejected: map the backend vendor to its FAMILY channel so Cloud
and DC both mint under the shared 'jira' provider/channel. The ticket-creation path a few lines below
ALREADY hard-codes validate_creation_channel('jira'), so the two paths in the same module are currently
inconsistent and the identity path is the wrong one. Widening CREATION_CHANNELS is REJECTED: it forks
the store vocabulary per deployment, contradicts the epic's shared-identity decision, fragments one
human's identity across deployments, and pulls in the migration + compatibility gate this epic avoids.

Four ACs added. Plan attestation is invalidated by this edit, so review-plan is being re-run.

SEPARATELY, and NOT resolved: AC8 requires asserting 'a populated RemoteRef.instance'. RemoteRef is
NEVER CONSTRUCTED IN PRODUCTION CODE — grep across src/ finds only the frozen dataclass definition and
docstrings; the sole constructions in the whole repo are in tests (backend_support.py:174 and the
value-equality contract test). So no reconcile pass can populate it and that half of AC8 is not
satisfiable as written. Flagging rather than quietly asserting the half that works.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
MECHANISM CORRECTED before implementing — my scope note for the folded-in bug 5f48 was wrong, and the
correction changes what the fix must do.

I wrote that every inbound DC ghost-identity mint FAILS silently. It does not: the mint is never
ATTEMPTED. _ensure_inbound_assignee_identity (apply_inbound_records.py:50) returns early unless the
assignee carries a non-empty accountId, and identity_model.py:26 states DC has no accountId at all —
DC users carry name/key. It is called with the raw Jira user object (:155, :321), so the DC path exits
at the guard.

That splits the work into TWO defects that COMPOUND:
 (a) ACTIVE: DC inbound assignees mint no identity at all — the guard demands an identifier DC never
     supplies. Cloud gets ghost identities; DC silently does not. Nothing raises.
 (b) LATENT: the ValueError is real (proven at the API) but unreachable while the guard short-circuits.
     It fires the moment someone teaches the guard DC's name — i.e. the moment someone fixes (a) ALONE.
     And since the call sits in 'except Exception: # best-effort ghost mint' logged at DEBUG, that
     one-line fix converts a silent no-op into a SWALLOWED EXCEPTION — strictly harder to diagnose.

So neither half alone is a fix, and the obvious fix to (a) makes things worse. Both land together.
Added an AC that pins exactly this: with the guard fixed but the channel unmapped, the mint raises and
is swallowed. That test is what stops a future contributor from splitting them.

HOW I CAUGHT IT: I was about to write the RED test and checked whether the DC path actually REACHES the
failing call, instead of assuming my API-level repro implied reachability. It did not. A repro proving
a function rejects an input says nothing about whether that input ever arrives — the same
check-the-quantifier failure the handoff warned about, caught this time before it reached code.

The in-flight review-plan was killed rather than left to certify the wrong rationale; re-running.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
LIVE TIER RAN IN CI (GitHub Actions run 30604756524, job 'jira DC harness smoke') — and it FOUND A
REAL DEFECT. Result: 2 failed, 12 passed, 1 error.

THE HEADLINE: a WRITING reconcile pass against a real Jira DC instance CRASHES.

    ERROR: reconcile_once raised: 'JiraDataCenterTransport' object has no attribute
    'set_entity_property'

dry-run passes (my test_dc_reconcile_pass_raises_no_unhandled_exception is green); only the writing
path dies. Filed as [rebar:a357-b747-ece9-4cf5].

ROOT CAUSE, which is the interesting part: set_entity_property is called from THREE core sites
(dispatch_one.py:321, binding_store.py:517, apply_inbound_records.py:279), implemented in exactly ONE
(adapters/jira/acli_rest.py:266, Cloud) — and is NOT A MEMBER OF THE TicketTransport PROTOCOL. The
port declares only create_issue/get_issue/update_issue/transition_issue_by_name/add_label/
search_issues. So the core depends on a transport method the port never states.

That is why everything I did this story passed while the real thing was broken: isinstance(x,
TicketTransport) is satisfied without it, the contract suite never calls it, and 1636 unit tests are
green. Making the DC backend Backend-conformant — this story's core work — was necessary and is NOT
sufficient, because the Protocol is not a faithful statement of what the core requires. Conformance to
an incomplete port proves less than it appears to. Same class as J6's add_label defect.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS STORY'S ACs: the three [operator-attested] live criteria are NOT met and I am not
marking them met:
  - full reconcile pass converges + repeated pass writes nothing  -> FAILED (exit 1)
  - DC-created ticket provenance                                   -> FAILED (same crash)
  - zero unhandled exceptions                                      -> PASSED for dry-run only
The epic cannot honestly claim 'Jira Server/DC support' while a DC deployment cannot complete a
writing pass.

SECOND FINDING, and this one MY tests caused: [rebar:f391-806b-938f-45d8]. The run also errored at
setup of an UNRELATED, previously-passing test with
'UserTokenLimitExceededException: You can't create more than 10 tokens'. jira_dc_pat
(conftest.py:355) is FUNCTION-scoped with no teardown, so every consuming test mints a new PAT and
never deletes it; Jira DC caps a user at 10. My three new tests transitively request it and pushed the
session over. The bug was latent; my tests made it fire — and it surfaces in a module nobody touched,
which is exactly the misattribution that burns a debugging session.

WHAT WENT RIGHT: this is the live tier doing precisely its job. Every unit-level signal was green; only
driving a real instance exposed it. That is the argument for this story having had a live AC at all.

compiled_state.description:
# J7 — Assemble `JiraDataCenterBackend` and hold it to the backend contract suite

## Context / Problem

With the shared Jira-family layer, the two codecs, the two identity models, and the DC transport in place, the
DC backend itself is an assembly — but it must actually be *proven*. ADR 0035's "Proof-of-seam" makes the
backend-agnostic contract suite the artifact that certifies a backend, and
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_contract.py` parametrizes its `backend` fixture over
`["fake", "jira"]`. PR #120 added registry and transport tests but never touched that fixture, so its new
backend was never held to the port contract at all.

## What J6 already landed (scope correction, measured against `origin/main` fdc2695a1)

This story's Scope was written before J6 [rebar:9fd4-a94c-156e-4a56] executed, and J6's change 1049 delivered
more than this plan anticipated. Verified against the merged tree, NOT assumed:

* `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` **already exists** (273 LOC) with `JiraDataCenterBackend`, the
  `@register("jira-datacenter")` factory, and `_search_users_by_username`;
* `adapters/__init__.py` **already imports** the DC backend (line 16), so `select_backend("jira-datacenter")`
  resolves — J6 pins that with its own registry test.

So this story is NOT "write the backend". It is the part J6 could not do: **make the backend reachable through
config, make it actually satisfy the `Backend` port, and hold it to the contract suite.**

## The port-conformance defect this story must fix (measured, not inferred)

`isinstance(JiraDataCenterBackend(transport=...), Backend)` is **`False` on merged `main` today.** The
`Backend` `@runtime_checkable` Protocol (`_backend.py`) requires nine members; the DC backend defines seven and
is missing **`query_project`** and **`assert_env_ready`**, both of which Cloud's `JiraBackend` implements
(`adapters/jira/backend.py:162` and `:169`). Probed directly:

```
vendor True | project True | query_project False | assert_env_ready False
```

This is a production defect, not test bookkeeping, and it is precisely what the contract suite exists to catch
— J6's registry test passed while the backend does not satisfy the port:

* **`query_project`** is the backend's configured READ/query scope, with NO create-time default applied. The
  inbound fetcher scopes its search to it and **fails closed on an empty/invalid value rather than querying
  every project** (bug 626d). Absent, the fetcher raises `AttributeError` on any DC inbound pass.
* **`assert_env_ready`** is the fail-fast that raises the neutral `BackendEnvError` naming the missing
  connection essential BEFORE the transport is used in bootstrap-band execution, instead of a cryptic
  downstream failure (ticket 97f2).

Adding `jira-datacenter` to the contract fixture makes `test_isinstance_backend_facade` go RED until both are
implemented. The suite is the oracle: **the fix belongs in `backend.py`, and no assertion may be weakened to
accommodate the backend.**

## Approach

Widen `reconciler.backend`'s `_as_choice` set to `{"jira", "jira-datacenter"}` and update the field comment,
closing the registered-but-unreachable gap. Implement the two missing `Backend` members on
`JiraDataCenterBackend`, mirroring Cloud's semantics but resolving through DC's own
`resolve_jira_datacenter_settings()` (`adapters/jira_datacenter/settings.py`) rather than Cloud's
`acli_subprocess.resolve_jira_settings`:

* `query_project` returns `resolve_jira_datacenter_settings().project` with **no default substituted** — empty
  when unset, so the fetcher fails closed exactly as Cloud does;
* `assert_env_ready` raises `BackendEnvError` naming whichever of the DC connection essentials is missing —
  the base URL (`[tool.rebar.reconciler].base_url`) and the env-only `JIRA_PAT` — matching Cloud's message
  shape ("missing … configuration: …").

`JiraDataCenterBackend` already composes the shared layer [rebar:62d9-9f6d-ecf4-4743] with `WikiTextCodec`
[rebar:aac8-b283-22c1-4e66], `NameIdentity` [rebar:0a94-e104-7304-4d85], and the DC transport
[rebar:9fd4-a94c-156e-4a56]; it advertises `SupportsLinks`, `SupportsComments`, and `SupportsAbsenceProbe`, and
deliberately **not** `SupportsIncremental` — DC gets a full inbound scan in v1, since incremental fetch is an
optimization with its own correctness surface and no client need yet. This story asserts that omission so it
cannot be added by accident.

Provenance follows the epic's decision: DC-created tickets carry the shared `jira` creation channel and
`jira-` local-id prefix, with the deployment distinguished by `RemoteRef.instance`. Nothing in the store
vocabulary changes, so no migration and no compatibility gate are involved.

**Then extend `test_backend_contract.py`'s fixture params to include the DC backend** (constructed with an
injected fake transport, exactly as `JiraBackend` already is at that fixture), so every generic port assertion
runs against it.

**Alternative rejected:** adapter-local tests only (PR #120). They prove the adapter does what its author
expected, not that it satisfies the port the core drives.

## Scope

- **`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py`** — implement the two missing
  `Backend` members, `query_project` and `assert_env_ready` (see the port-conformance section above). This is
  the file the contract suite's RED test drives; it was absent from an earlier draft of this Scope.
- **`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py`** — the inbound identity path derives
  BOTH the identity provider and its creation channel from the backend's vendor string
  (`vendor = select_backend(load_config()).vendor`, then
  `ensure_identity_for(vendor, …, creation_channel=vendor)`). For DC that vendor is
  `"jira-datacenter"`, which is NOT in the store vocabulary
  (`CREATION_CHANNELS = {cli, mcp, python, jira, import, unknown}`), so the mint raises `ValueError`.
  Measured on a scratch repo:

      creation_channel='jira'            ext=acct-cloud -> returned '4802-2404-6de4-4167'
      creation_channel='jira-datacenter' ext=acct-dc    -> ValueError: invalid creation_channel

  **TWO defects here, and they compound — the second is a trap set by the obvious fix to the first.**

  *(a) The active gap.* `_ensure_inbound_assignee_identity` (`:50`) returns early unless the assignee
  object carries a non-empty `accountId`, and `adapters/jira_family/identity_model.py:26` states that
  **DC has no accountId at all** — DC users carry `name`/`key` (REST v2). It is called with the RAW
  Jira user object (`:155`, `:321`), so on a DC deployment it exits at the guard. Result: Cloud mints
  ghost identities on inbound; **DC silently mints none**. Nothing raises — the mint is never
  attempted.

  *(b) The latent landmine behind it.* The channel rejection above is real but currently UNREACHABLE,
  because the `accountId` guard short-circuits first. It fires the moment anyone teaches the guard
  DC's `name` — i.e. the moment someone fixes (a) alone. And because the call sits inside
  `except Exception:  # best-effort ghost mint; never fail the inbound apply`, logged at DEBUG, that
  one-line "fix" converts a silent no-op into a SWALLOWED EXCEPTION, which is strictly harder to
  diagnose. This is epic AC6's premise exactly: the pass still converges either way.

  So the fix is BOTH halves together, and neither alone is sufficient: accept DC's `name` as the
  external id when `accountId` is absent, AND map the backend vendor to its FAMILY channel so the
  resulting mint validates. The ticket-creation path a few lines below ALREADY hard-codes
  `create_data["creation_channel"] = validate_creation_channel("jira")`, so the identity path is the
  inconsistent one. **Do NOT widen `CREATION_CHANNELS`**: that forks the store vocabulary per
  deployment, contradicting the epic's shared-identity decision, fragmenting one human's identity
  across deployments, and dragging in a migration + compatibility gate the epic explicitly avoids.
  **This story is the right home** because its `reconciler.backend` widening is what first makes a DC
  deployment configurable at all. (Folded in from bug [rebar:5f48-244c-7063-42d0], whose original
  mechanism description was corrected on that ticket.)
- `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — widen the `reconciler.backend` `_as_choice` set (currently `{"jira"}`) and
  update the field comment. **Use a symbol search, not the line number** that an earlier draft of this Scope
  carried (`:697`): the file has changed since, and the validator now sits near `:604`. J6 already owns the DC
  *connection* settings in this file (TLS/`allow_insecure`, `ca_bundle`, `resolved_statuses`); this story owns
  ONLY the backend-choice widening.
- **`tests/unit/test_config_reconciler_backend.py`** — the dedicated config-validator module (it already
  exists, 2.5K, and already covers default/explicit-jira/unknown-key/env-override). The new
  `jira-datacenter` load case, the env-override case, and the `"jira-server"` rejection case all belong HERE,
  alongside their siblings — not in a new module. Note its existing
  `test_unknown_backend_rejected_at_config_load` asserts `"jira" in str(exc.value)`, which still holds after
  the widening, so it needs no edit.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_backend_contract.py` — fixture params.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/backend_support.py` — **decided, not deferred:** the existing `FakeTransport`
  is what the DC fixture uses. It already satisfies every `TicketTransport` member the contract assertions
  reach. It lacks `probe_remote`, which the backend delegates, but NO contract assertion calls it, and
  `SupportsAbsenceProbe` conformance is satisfied by the *backend's* own `probe_remote`, not the transport's.
  So: **add a one-line `probe_remote` to `FakeTransport`** (so the delegation is exercisable and the fake
  matches the surface the DC backend delegates to) and do **not** introduce a rival DC-specific fake.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_family_boundary_heldout.py` — the reciprocal import rule. The J2
  checker already rejects `adapters/jira/` importing `adapters/jira_datacenter/` (the `_is_within(package,
  _JIRA)` branch in `_violations`), but there is **no rule for the other direction**: a DC module importing
  `adapters/jira/` passes today. That is the half this story adds.
- `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml` — add `jira` to the clean-core-wheel absent-module list at line 86
  (today `langchain`, `langgraph`, `anthropic`, `inspect_ai`, `opentelemetry`). Verified safe: `jira` is
  declared ONLY in the `jira-datacenter` extra (`pyproject.toml:168`); the base `dependencies` are just
  `pyyaml`, `jsonschema`, `referencing`, and the `"jira"` at `pyproject.toml:24` is a *keyword*, not a dep.
- **`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py`** (new) — note the path. An earlier draft said
  `tests/live_jira_dc/`, which does not exist; J5 [rebar:c97f-90ae-4976-47c7] landed the harness under
  `tests/external/`, the only tier fenced off from per-commit CI. A live test outside it is collected by the
  default suite on runners with no Docker, no Jira and no egress, breaking CI for everyone. Landing under the
  right path also inherits the tier's three mechanisms: the auto-applied `external` marker, the
  `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1` opt-in, and the module-level `_live_jira_ready` sentinel that enrols the module in the
  all-skip canary — so this file MUST define one. J6 additionally established that a live module must FAIL
  LOUDLY (not skip) when the harness is reachable but the `[jira-datacenter]` extra is absent, because the
  canary counts collected-vs-executed globally and a sibling module's executing tests will otherwise mask an
  all-skip; **reuse the exact guard already written in `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_transport.py`**
  (`_live_jira_ready` / `_jira_extra_installed` / `_extra_missing_but_harness_up` /
  `_fail_if_extra_missing_while_harness_is_up`) rather than reinventing it.
  **Local-side provisioning is settled, not left to the executor:** a reconcile pass needs a local ticket
  store, a git repo and a rebar config, which the DC harness conftest does not provision (it owns only the
  Jira side — project, PAT, issue teardown). The `rebar_repo` fixture that
  `tests/external/test_reconcile_live.py` uses is defined in **`tests/external/conftest.py:159`**, the PARENT
  conftest, so `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` **inherits it by ordinary pytest conftest inheritance**. Use it
  directly together with the DC harness's `jira_dc_project` / `jira_dc_pat` fixtures. No new
  `rebar_repo`-equivalent is to be written.
  **But `rebar_repo` alone is NOT sufficient, and the wiring is specified here rather than left to the
  executor.** That fixture calls `rebar.init_repo()` and writes NO `[tool.rebar.reconciler]` config, so the
  reconcile subprocess would have no backend, no base URL and no credential — it would fail at config-load or
  silently drive the Cloud backend. The test MUST therefore, before reconciling:
  1. write a `rebar.toml` into the `rebar_repo` root containing `[reconciler]` with
     `backend = "jira-datacenter"`, `base_url = <the harness base URL>`, and **`allow_insecure = true`** —
     the latter is REQUIRED, not optional: the harness is `http://localhost:2990/jira`
     (`tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py:56`, overridable via `JIRA_DC_BASE_URL`), and J6's TLS
     validator in `_config_schema.py` REJECTS a non-`https` base URL at config-load time unless
     `allow_insecure` is set. Also write `[jira]` with `project = <jira_dc_project>`, which is where
     `resolve_jira_datacenter_settings()` reads the project from;
  2. `monkeypatch.setenv("JIRA_PAT", jira_dc_pat)` — `jira_dc_pat` returns a raw token STRING and sets no
     environment variable itself. This does reach the child process: `rebar._engine.engine_env` builds the
     subprocess environment as `dict(os.environ)` (`_engine.py:93`), so the PAT propagates.

## Testing

Contract tier for the port, plus a live end-to-end pass on the J5 harness [rebar:c97f-90ae-4976-47c7] because this story is
the point at which the whole assembly first drives a real instance.

- contract: every existing assertion in `test_backend_contract.py` passes with the DC backend in the fixture
  params, unmodified — the suite is the oracle and must not be weakened to accommodate the new backend.
- port conformance (RED-first): `test_isinstance_backend_facade` is asserted to FAIL before `query_project` /
  `assert_env_ready` exist and PASS after — the defect is demonstrated, not merely fixed.
- `query_project` / `assert_env_ready` behaviour, in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/`: `query_project` returns
  the configured project and returns **empty** (not a default) when unset, so the fetcher's fail-closed
  contract holds; `assert_env_ready` raises `BackendEnvError` naming each missing essential and returns
  cleanly when all are present.
- capability: `isinstance` checks confirm `Backend`, `SupportsLinks`, `SupportsComments`,
  `SupportsAbsenceProbe`, and confirm it is NOT `SupportsIncremental` (the deliberate omission, asserted so it
  cannot be added by accident).
- config, in `tests/unit/test_config_reconciler_backend.py`: `reconciler.backend = "jira-datacenter"` loads;
  the `REBAR_RECONCILER_BACKEND=jira-datacenter` env override resolves; an unknown key still raises
  `ConfigError` naming the valid choices.
- import contract: the new reciprocal rule has TEETH — a synthetic DC-imports-Cloud source is asserted to be
  flagged, mirroring how J2's `test_checker_flags_a_synthetic_violation` proves its own direction, with the
  permitted `jira_datacenter -> jira_family` direction retained as a negative control.
- live end-to-end: a full reconcile pass against the harness creates a remote issue from a local ticket,
  round-trips a status change and a comment inbound, and a second pass is a **no-op** — idempotence is the
  postcondition that proves convergence rather than mere writing.
- provenance oracle: asserted in the **live** module (`test_reconcile_pass.py`), since only a real pass
  produces a genuinely DC-created local ticket — a DC-created local ticket has `creation_channel == "jira"`
  and a `jira-`-prefixed id, and its `RemoteRef.instance` names the DC deployment, pinning the epic's
  shared-identity decision.
- error path: a transport failure PROPAGATES — asserted at the unit tier with `pytest.raises`, driving a fake
  transport that raises on a write. **One behaviour, one assertion style:** the criterion is satisfied by
  propagation only; a caught-and-logged variant does NOT satisfy it, so there is no "or" for an executor to
  resolve.
- zero-unhandled-exceptions mechanism (live): **not `caplog`.** `rebar.reconcile()` runs the reconciler in a
  SUBPROCESS (`subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True)`, `src/rebar/_lib_ops.py:114`), and `caplog` hooks
  only the *test* process's `logging`, so it can never see those records — and on the success path
  `reconcile()` returns parsed stdout JSON and discards stderr entirely. The live test therefore invokes the
  reconciler subprocess DIRECTLY — the same argv `_lib_ops.reconcile` builds
  (`[sys.executable, "-m", "rebar_reconciler", "--mode", <mode>, "--repo-root", <root>]`, with
  `env=rebar._engine.engine_env(root)`) — with `capture_output=True`, then asserts on the captured streams.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `JiraDataCenterBackend` implements `query_project`, and `isinstance(backend, Backend)` is asserted
      `True`
- [ ] `query_project` returns the EMPTY string when the project is unset — no create-time default
      substituted — preserving the inbound fetcher's fail-closed contract (bug 626d)
- [ ] `JiraDataCenterBackend` implements `assert_env_ready`, which raises `BackendEnvError` naming each
      missing DC connection essential and returns cleanly when all are present
- [ ] `test_backend_contract.py`'s fixture includes `jira-datacenter` and the suite passes with no assertion
      weakened (`git diff` shows params-only change to that file)
- [ ] a test asserts the backend is NOT an instance of `SupportsIncremental`
- [ ] `FakeTransport` in `backend_support.py` exposes `probe_remote`, and a test asserts the DC backend's
      `probe_remote` DELEGATES to it (observed via the fake's recorded `calls`)
- [ ] [operator-attested] a full reconcile pass against the J5 harness converges, and an immediately repeated pass writes nothing
      (idempotence), with both pass logs attached as a ticket comment
- [ ] a DC-created ticket is asserted — in `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py` — to carry
      the SHARED `creation_channel == "jira"`, pinning the epic's decision that a DC deployment does not
      fork the store vocabulary.
      **The `RemoteRef.instance` half of this criterion is deliberately NOT asserted here, and the reason
      is a finding, not a concession:** `RemoteRef` is never constructed in production code. Across the
      repo, `src/` contains only the frozen dataclass definition (`_backend.py:60`) and docstrings; the
      sole constructions are two test helpers (`backend_support.py:174`, `test_backend_contract.py:96`).
      No reconcile pass can populate `instance`, so asserting it would require building that machinery —
      a different story, filed as [rebar:6a91-7429-e521-4a2e] with the design question (deriving
      `instance` from a mutable base URL silently re-identifies every ticket when an operator moves the
      instance). Asserting only the half that works while quoting the whole criterion is exactly the
      false-confidence this epic's gates exist to prevent.
- [ ] `reconciler.backend = "jira-datacenter"` loads, asserted in
      `tests/unit/test_config_reconciler_backend.py`
- [ ] the `REBAR_RECONCILER_BACKEND=jira-datacenter` env override resolves, asserted in the same module
- [ ] `reconciler.backend = "jira-server"` still raises `ConfigError` listing the valid choices
- [ ] the import-contract test from J2 is EXTENDED to cover the now-existing `adapters/jira_datacenter/`
      package: no module under it imports from `adapters/jira/`, and `adapters/jira_family/` imports from
      neither adapter — this is the reciprocal half J2 could not assert because the package did not exist yet
- [ ] `jira` is added to the absent-module list in `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml`'s clean-core-wheel
      check (which today covers only `langchain`, `langgraph`, `anthropic`, `inspect_ai`, `opentelemetry`), so
      a future change that leaks the DC dependency into the base install fails CI
- [ ] the live bidirectional pass asserts ZERO unhandled exceptions by invoking the reconciler SUBPROCESS
      directly (`[sys.executable, "-m", "rebar_reconciler", "--mode", …, "--repo-root", …]` under
      `engine_env`, `capture_output=True`) and asserting `returncode == 0`, `"Traceback" not in stderr`, and
      `mutation_failures == 0` in the parsed stdout envelope — `caplog` is NOT usable here because the
      reconciler runs in a subprocess (`_lib_ops.py:114`), and a swallowed exception can still converge
      (epic AC6)
- [ ] a DC transport failure on a write PROPAGATES out of the call, asserted with `pytest.raises` against a
      fake transport that raises — it is not swallowed into a converged pass
- [ ] an inbound apply under the DC backend MINTS a ghost identity for a DC-shaped assignee (one with
      `name` and NO `accountId`), asserted by a test that FAILS against today's code — where the mint is
      not merely broken but never attempted, because the `accountId` guard returns early
- [ ] a test pins the compound failure: with the `accountId` guard fixed but the channel NOT mapped, the
      mint raises `ValueError: invalid creation_channel 'jira-datacenter'` and that exception is
      SWALLOWED at DEBUG — proving why the two halves must land together and cannot be split
- [ ] that identity is minted under the SHARED `jira` provider/creation channel, matching what the
      ticket-creation path in the same module already hard-codes
- [ ] the test asserts the mint SUCCEEDED — not merely that no exception escaped — because the call site
      swallows every exception at DEBUG, so "nothing raised" is true even when nothing worked
- [ ] `CREATION_CHANNELS` is UNCHANGED: no per-deployment vocabulary fork, no migration, no
      compatibility gate
